recall_prompt: Say how you would find r when 12 P r is 1320.
insider_note: The same product 12 · 11 · 10 = 1320 appears in the ⁿP₃ twin, but here the unknown is r: count the factors written, 3 — the last factor 10 is not r.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write 1320 as factors counting down from 12
steps.margin_note: First mark. ¹²Pᵣ = 12 · 11 · 10 · … with r factors. Divide 1320 by 12, then 11, then 10 until 1 is reached.

recall.must_convey: That 12 P r is a product of r factors starting at 12 and counting down, and 1320 is 12 times 11 times 10.
accept: twelve P r is twelve into eleven into ten and so on for r factors and thirteen twenty is twelve times eleven times ten
divide thirteen twenty by twelve then eleven then ten
thirteen twenty is twelve times eleven times ten, three factors
thirteen twenty ni twelve eleven ten ga rayali
count how many factors from twelve downward make thirteen twenty

steps.why: In ¹²Pᵣ the first factor is fixed at 12, so the unknown is how many factors are taken. Dividing 1320 by 12, then 11, then 10 answers that directly.
common_mistakes: Writing ¹²Pᵣ = 12!/r! — the correct form is 12!/(12 − r)!.

steps.label: Count the factors and state r
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three factors, so ¹²Pᵣ = ¹²P₃ and r = 3.

recall.must_convey: That there are three factors, so r = 3.
accept: three factors so r is three
twelve P r is twelve P three so r is three
the number of factors is r, which is three

steps.why: r counts the factors in the product, not the last factor; the last factor is 12 − r + 1 = 10, which confirms r = 3.
common_mistakes: Answering r = 10, the last factor, instead of the number of factors.
